issue.title: usage: a web search sent to Kimi Code's or WorkBuddy's search service, or to a search API, leaves no row in Usage › Requests
issue.body:
neiko (Discord) asked whether magpie's helper requests can reach a provider without the user seeing it. Most can't go unseen: a model search, an image description and a routing classification go through `s.serve`, so each one is a request-log row with Kind `web_search`, `vision` or `routing`. Three web-search paths send their own HTTP request and never write a row:

- Kimi Code's search service: `kimiSearch`, internal/gateway/search_kimi.go:101-125. It does `s.client.Do` directly; `s.metered` only counts RPM (rpm.go:246).
- WorkBuddy's search: `wbSearch`, internal/gateway/search_workbuddy.go (POST to `origin+wbSearchPath`, line ~63).
- The search APIs (Tavily/Brave/…): `apiSearch`, internal/gateway/search_api.go. They run first when Search first = API, last otherwise, or alone when Searcher is off (search.go:667-707).

So a user who asks "what did magpie send to Kimi/my search key" finds nothing in Requests, though each of these spends the plan's or the key's allowance. Found by reading the code at ffe493773; not reproduced with a real account.

Fix direction: write each one as a request-log row under its provider (or the search API's name) with Kind `web_search`, as magpie's model searches are. Whether it counts toward totals the way a model search does needs deciding: it has no tokens, only a call.

comments.body:
Confirmed: `kimiSearch`, `wbSearch` and `askSearchAPI` send their own HTTP request, never go through `s.serve`, and so never reach the row writer - Usage > Requests had nothing for a search a user's plan or search key paid for.

Fixed on [fix/3528-search-usage-rows](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/3528-search-usage-rows) (`f6064d5d`, on `c0985122`): each of the three paths writes one row through a shared `logSearchCall` - `Kind: web_search`, the provider's id (or the search API's `Name()`), host, status, milliseconds and the error when it failed - on success and on failure alike, via a `defer`.

On the decision the issue leaves open: the row is counted as a call, like the model-search `web_search` row, but its tokens, cache and cost are all zero, so no total changes; nothing in the counting path was altered. One consequence worth naming: a turn that searched now has one more ledger row, exactly as a turn with a model search always had, so `usage_cache_zero_split_test.go`'s expectation now looks at the turn's own row.

RED -> GREEN, re-run independently here:
- clean base `c0985122` with only the new test: all three subtests fail with `0 rows written, want 1` (Kimi Code's search service, WorkBuddy's search service, a search API).
- at the head: `TestSearchesWriteARequestRow` passes and the surrounding search tests still pass (62 in the filtered run). Full `go test ./internal/gateway` (261.8s) fails only `TestClaudeClientCacheAbsentUnchanged`, red on the clean base too; `go vet`, the three builds and `gofmt -l` are clean.

Limits: the Recent-calls ring is not written (it wants an agent protocol and a model, which these calls have not); a path that fails before sending (masking, WorkBuddy's `Sign`) leaves a row with status 0; only in-package fakes were used - no real Kimi, WorkBuddy or search-API key was called.

c420559fd (v0.1.2308): each ask of a search API, and each search sent to Kimi Code's or WorkBuddy's own search service, is now a row of Usage › Requests (badge "Search API" / "Web search"): vendor, host, outcome, time. Listed only, never counted in totals, not exported, no query text. Not tried with real Tavily/Kimi/WorkBuddy accounts yet, so this stays open until the reporter confirms.

b09349d17 (v0.1.2309), from the same report: Settings › Models › Web search › "Models that search by themselves" can be set to magpie's search, so a provider that searches by itself is answered by the searcher/search APIs instead. Codex sign-in turns relayed as sent keep their native search.
